after_drawn_game_first_player.suggestion: No official rule. Use the game-1 procedure (seeded random chooser) for the next game.

asia_differences: The English (Asia) BO3 page matches the US page. The Asia floor rules' final time-out tiebreak is one round of rock-paper-scissors instead of 'both players lose' (US Sanctioned Floor Rules). This only matters with a clock.
deck_between_games: same validated deck every game (no sideboarding in the simulator)

draws.game_level_rule: CR 11-2-1: all players who meet a defeat condition at a rules-management check are defeated together. CR 1-2-1 gives a winner only when exactly one player is defeated, so simultaneous defeat has no winner.
draws.official_tournament_handling: Swiss: a drawn match scores 1 point (TRM 3.4.2, 5.4). Single elimination and top cut (the BO3 setting): 'If there is a tie due to all players fulfilling loss conditions simultaneously, the current turn-player loses the game' (TRM 5.2).
draws.simulator_suggestion: Report simultaneous defeat as a game draw in per-game statistics. In BO3, apply the TRM 5.2 top-cut rule (current turn player loses) so every game has a winner and a match ends within 3 games. Lead to confirm.

game_1_first_player: random method; the winner chooses Player One (CR 6-2-1-4, TRM 4.6)

ignored_by_simulator.extra_turns_and_end_of_round: Official: time runs out in P1's turn -> 3 extra turns, in P2's turn -> 2, then tiebreaks (TRM 5.2). Not modelled: no clock.
ignored_by_simulator.sideboarding: Official BO3 allows a 10-card sideboard swapped between games; not modelled.
ignored_by_simulator.time_limit: Official BO3: 60 minutes per match, extra time 10 minutes (TRM 3.5); no clock in the simulator.

later_games_first_player: the player who lost the previous game chooses Player One and Player Two

sources.quote: In this match format, up to three one-on-one games are played within a 60-minute time limit, and the first player to win two games wins the match.

During the first game, Player One and Player Two are determined using a random method such as rock paper scissors. During the second and third games, Players One and Two are chosen by the player who lost the previous game.
Matches are conducted using the standard rules for two-player matches.
In a best-of-three game match, the player who loses the preceding game chooses whether to go first in the next game.
If there is a tie due to all players fulfilling loss conditions simultaneously, the current turn-player loses the game, and the opponent is declared the winner.
For Professional level events, Tournament Organizers should use a best-of-one game match format during qualifying rounds and Best-of-three match format for top cut.
